title: Advanced CP techniques: game theory, matrix expo, MITM, ternary search, sqrt / Mo
relevance: Medium — rarely the literal OA template, but Nim-XOR / “nth term of recurrence” / “n≤40 subset sum” / unimodal optimization show up in harder screens; primarily Candidate Master rating-builders Striver never covers.
company_notes: Two players take from piles / subtract a size set → who wins: Nim XOR or short Grundy (CSES Nim I/II). Compute the n-th Fibonacci / ways for length 10^18 → matrix expo (fib / tiling / graph walks). Array size ≤40, count subsets with sum = X → meet-in-the-middle (CSES MITM), not 2^n DP. Minimize the maximum of a unimodal cost over a real parameter → ternary search (Meeting Place / Motarack).

phases.goal: Map the prompt to game theory, matrix expo, MITM, ternary search, or Mo/sqrt from constraints and wording.

must_hit.point: Impartial pile / subtract-a-set games → Nim XOR or short Grundy; multi-pile combines via XOR of Grundy/nimbers.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names pile take/subtract who-wins and reaches for Nim XOR or Grundy rather than ad-hoc casework.

must_hit.point: Linear recurrence or fixed-size DP transition with huge n (nth Fib / ways for length 10^18 / graph walks of length k) → matrix exponentiation.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties huge index or path-count length to encoding a transition matrix and powering it.

must_hit.point: Array size n≤40 with subset-sum style ask → meet-in-the-middle; plain 2^n is too big.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says split into halves and enum 2^{n/2} instead of full subset DP when n≤40.

must_hit.point: Unimodal cost on a continuous or discrete line → ternary (or BS on derivative); many offline range queries with add/remove-friendly state → Mo / sqrt.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates unimodal optimize-a-parameter from offline Mo/block range queries.

probes: What constraint or phrase makes you pick Nim/Grundy, matrix expo, MITM, ternary, or Mo instead of plain DP or binary search?

hints.1: Look at n, whether the ask is who-wins / nth term / subset sum / unimodal min-max / offline ranges.
hints.2: Piles→game XOR; huge linear recurrence→matrix; n≤40 subsets→MITM; unimodal f→ternary; offline add/remove ranges→Mo.
hints.3: Say: pile/subtract who-wins→Nim/Grundy; Fib/tiling/walks at 10^18→matrix expo; n≤40 sum=X→MITM not 2^n; unimodal real parameter→ternary; offline [L,R] with add/remove→Mo.

phases.goal: State the correct template for the chosen tool before coding.

must_hit.point: Impartial game: terminal = lose; win if any move to a lose; g(s)=mex{g(t): s→t}; sum of independent games = XOR of Grundies; g=0 is second-player win.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Defines mex Grundy, XOR composition, and g=0 ⇒ second player.

must_hit.point: Standard Nim: g(pile)=size so xor≠0 ⇒ first wins; subtraction-{1..k}: g(n)=n mod (k+1) then XOR piles.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives Nim size-grundy / xor≠0 first-win and subtraction mod (k+1).

must_hit.point: Matrix expo: build transition M with state_{i+1}=M·state_i; answer from M^n · state_0 (always mod); path counts use adjacency / DP-transition matrix to power k.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes the state transition matrix story and mentions walks as A^k.

must_hit.point: MITM: split n in half, enumerate 2^{n/2} subset sums (or XORs), sort one side, binary-search / hash complements.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes half-split enum plus sort/hash combine.

must_hit.point: Ternary only on strictly unimodal f; Mo: block size ~√n (or n/√q), sort by (L/B, R), maintain add(i)/remove(i); if add/remove is unnatural prefer sqrt blocks / rebuild.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States unimodal precondition for ternary and Mo block-sort vs plain sqrt blocks.

probes: For this prompt, walk through the exact template: Grundy/XOR, M^n, half-enum MITM, ternary shrink, or Mo add/remove.

hints.1: Name the state you XOR, the matrix you power, or how you split / search the line / move pointers.
hints.2: Game→mex+XOR; recurrence→M then M^n; MITM→two halves + sort; ternary→compare mid neighbors; Mo→block sort + add/remove.
hints.3: Outline: g=mex and XOR (g=0 second); M with state_{i+1}=M·state_i; split n, enum 2^{n/2}, match complements; ternary only if strictly unimodal; Mo sort (L/B,R) with add/remove.

phases.goal: Show concrete coding steps for matrix power, MITM combine, ternary shrink, and Mo pointers.

must_hit.point: Matrix template: multiply k×k matrices under mod and binary-exponentiate M to get M^n · state_0 (fib is the 2×2 case).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions modular matrix mul + binary expo of the transition, citing fib 2×2.

must_hit.point: MITM coding: enumerate all subset sums on each half, sort one half, binary-search complements to count or optimize (e.g. max sum mod m).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes two-half enum, sort one side, then search/hash for the partner.

must_hit.point: Ternary: floats run ~100–200 iters; discrete compare f(m) vs f(m+1) and shrink the side that is worse.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives float iteration budget and discrete neighbor-compare shrink.

must_hit.point: Mo: choose block ~√n (or n/√q), sort queries by (L/B, R), move [L,R] with add(i)/remove(i) updating answer in O(1) or O(log).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States block size, sort key, and pointer moves with add/remove.

probes: How do you actually code the matrix power, the two-half MITM combine, discrete ternary, or Mo add/remove?

hints.1: Pick one template and name the loops: matrix mul, half masks, mid vs mid+1, or L/R expands.
hints.2: Matrix: mul+binpow under mod; MITM: enum halves→sort→search; ternary: neighbor compare or ~100–200 float iters; Mo: sort (L/B,R) then add/remove.
hints.3: Say: power M with k×k mul mod; enum both halves’ 2^{n/2} sums and binary-search; shrink by f(m) vs f(m+1) (or ~100–200 float iters); Mo block-sort and move pointers with add/remove.

phases.goal: State the standard costs for matrix expo, MITM, and Mo.

must_hit.point: Matrix exponentiation of a k×k transition costs O(k³ log n).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Quotes O(k³ log n) for powering the transition.

must_hit.point: Meet-in-the-middle subset enumeration is O(n·2^{n/2}).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States O(n·2^{n/2}) for the half-split enum.

must_hit.point: Mo’s algorithm moves [L,R] in O((n+q)√n) with block-sorted offline queries.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives O((n+q)√n) for Mo pointer movement.

must_hit.point: Sqrt blocking: full blocks O(√n) with edges brute after per-block precompute.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions per-block aggregates, full blocks O(√n), edges brute.

probes: What are the complexities of matrix expo, MITM, and Mo, and why those formulas?

hints.1: Relate cost to matrix size k, half-size n/2, or block size ~√n.
hints.2: k×k mul × log n; two halves of size n/2; Mo block sort yields (n+q)√n pointer moves.
hints.3: Say: matrix O(k³ log n); MITM O(n·2^{n/2}); Mo O((n+q)√n); sqrt blocks full-block O(√n) plus edge brute.

phases.goal: Catch misuse of ternary, MITM, Grundy polarity, and Mo vs blocks.

must_hit.point: Ternary search only on strictly unimodal f; applying it to a non-unimodal cost is wrong.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Refuses ternary unless decrease-then-increase (strictly unimodal) is justified.

must_hit.point: On n≤40 subset-sum, do not ship 2^n DP—use meet-in-the-middle.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects full subset enum at n≤40 in favor of MITM.

must_hit.point: g=0 is second-player win; xor≠0 ⇒ first wins in standard Nim—do not flip polarity.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Correctly maps g=0 / xor=0 to second player and xor≠0 to first.

must_hit.point: When Mo’s add/remove is not natural, prefer sqrt blocking / rebuild instead of forcing Mo.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Chooses blocks/rebuild when the state is not add/remove-friendly.

probes: Where do people mis-apply ternary, ship 2^n at n≤40, flip Nim win/lose, or force Mo incorrectly?

hints.1: Check unimodality, the n≤40 branch, who wins when xor is 0, and whether add/remove exists.
hints.2: Ternary needs strict unimodal; n≤40→MITM; g=0/xor=0→second; Mo needs friendly add/remove else blocks.
hints.3: Strictly unimodal only for ternary; MITM not 2^n when n≤40; g=0 second / xor≠0 first; if add/remove unnatural use sqrt blocks/rebuild.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: When n≤40 and 2^n is too big, split halves, enumerate 2^{n/2} subset sums/XORs, and combine with sort/hash; reserve full 2^n only for much smaller n.

tradeoffs.topic: Mo’s algorithm vs sqrt blocking / rebuild
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Use Mo when queries are offline and the state has natural add(i)/remove(i); when add/remove is not natural, prefer per-block aggregates with full blocks O(√n) and edges brute, or rebuild.

tradeoffs.topic: ternary search vs binary search on derivative
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Both target unimodal cost on a line; ternary (or discrete f(m) vs f(m+1) shrink) searches the parameter directly, while BS on derivative is the alternate when a monotone derivative check is cleaner.
Single-position win/lose DP (W iff some move to L) is the first drill; multi-pile / independent sum games need Grundy nimbers and XOR (Nim I/II, Stair Game odd-index XOR).

For linear recurrence or fixed-size DP with huge n (Fib, tiling length 10^18, walks of length k), encode the transition as a k×k matrix and power in O(k³ log n) under mod instead of stepping one-by-one.

gotchas.trap: Running ternary search when f is not strictly unimodal.
gotchas.correction: Require decrease-then-increase (strictly unimodal); otherwise ternary can converge to a wrong local extremum—use another method.

gotchas.trap: Treating xor=0 / g=0 as a first-player win.
gotchas.correction: g=0 is second-player win; in standard Nim xor≠0 ⇒ first wins.

gotchas.trap: Solving n≤40 subset sum with plain 2^n DP.
gotchas.correction: Split into halves, enumerate 2^{n/2}, combine with sort/hash (CSES Meet in the Middle).

gotchas.trap: Forgetting modular arithmetic on matrix exponentiation.
gotchas.correction: Matrix expo answers are taken always mod (e.g. fib template mod 1e9+7).

gotchas.trap: Forcing Mo when the state has no natural add/remove.
gotchas.correction: Prefer sqrt blocking with per-block precompute (full blocks O(√n), edges brute) or rebuild.

gotchas.trap: In Stair Game, XORing every pile like plain Nim.
